Expand an AudioMoth triggered (T.WAV) file

Source: R/audiomothTWav.R
audiomothExpand.Rd

AudioMoth devices recording on a trigger, such as an amplitude threshold, write a single T.WAV file in which the periods that did not trigger a recording are left out. Each omitted period is replaced by a 512-byte encoded block recording its length, so that the original timing of the triggered recordings can be restored. This function restores them, returning either a Wave object or an ordinary WAV file in which the omitted periods are silence.

Usage

audiomothExpand(file, output = NULL, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

file

Path to the T.WAV file to expand

output

Path to write the expanded WAV file to. If NULL (the default) no file is written and a Wave object is returned instead.

overwrite

If TRUE an existing output file is replaced

Value

A Wave object, or, if output is given, the path to the written file (invisibly)

Details

Only mono 16-bit PCM files are supported, which is what AudioMoth devices produce. A file holding no encoded blocks is returned unchanged, so this is safe to call on any AudioMoth recording. Metadata chunks, including the GUANO chunk written by current firmware, are carried over to the expanded file, and are attached to a returned Wave object as a "guano" attribute, which guano() will read.

Writing to output streams the expanded file to disk, so a recording that expands to more than memory can hold can still be expanded. Returning a Wave object necessarily holds the whole expanded recording in memory.

A recording cut short by a recorder that lost power is reported with a warning classed truncatedAudio, or unwrittenAudioSize where the size of the audio was never written, and the audio that is there is expanded. Both are also classed audioFileWarning; see readAudio() for the warnings that share those classes and for handling one of them without silencing the rest.

References

Open Acoustic Devices (2021) AudioMoth Triggered T.WAV File Format. https://github.com/OpenAcousticDevices/Application-Notes

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Read a triggered recording into a Wave object
w <- audiomothExpand("20201103_112430T.WAV")

# Expand every triggered recording on a card, as the reference tool does
for (f in list.files(pattern="T\\.WAV$")) {
  audiomothExpand(f, sub("T\\.WAV$", ".WAV", f))
}
} # }
